# extract — fetch one page

Field names are the JSON body names; MCP clients see the same names in the
tool's `inputSchema`, so this file is a fallback for raw-HTTP calls and for
reading a `16002` message that names a field.

### `flowda_extract` · `POST /v1/extract`

Scope `extract` · `/v1` budget 130s · gateway pre-charge 1 credit.

| field | type | required | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| advanced_mode | boolean | no | Allow the fetch service to escalate based on page signals. · default `true` |
| country | string | no | Access region, two letters. |
| exclude_tags | array<string> | no | CSS selectors of nodes to drop. |
| formats | array<string> | no | Representations to produce; no duplicates. |
| headers | object<string, string> | no | Headers forwarded to the target site; forces a cache bypass and marks the URL for 48 hours. |
| include_tags | array<string> | no | CSS selectors of nodes to keep. |
| max_age_ms | integer | no | Maximum acceptable snapshot age; 0 forces a fresh fetch. · default `172800000` · range 0–172800000 |
| only_main_content | boolean | no | Keep the article body only. · default `true` |
| timeout_ms | integer | no | Budget for the whole call. · default `60000` · range 1000–120000 |
| url | string | yes | Absolute http(s) URL of the page to fetch. |
| wait_for_ms | integer | no | Extra wait after page load; must be at most half of timeout_ms. · default `0` · range 0–30000 |

Body field names are identical for `application/json` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
